newsitem.title: BANGLADESH: Bangladesh PM Hasina vows to fight poverty.
newsitem.headline: Bangladesh PM Hasina vows to fight poverty.

text.p: Bangladesh Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina, facing opposition threats to cut her term short, said on Sunday the main aims of her five-month-old government were to end poverty, strengthen democracy and achieve quick industrialisation.
"The main aim of my government is to free the nation from the clutches of hunger, malnutrition and unemployment," she told a huge rally in Dhaka.

"We are working day and night to achieve these goals. We will reach the fruits of independence to every doorsteps...just keep faith in me," she told cheering and waving supporters at the rally, organised by the ruling Awami League to mark the silver jubilee of Bangladesh's independence.
Hasina's father Sheikh Mujibur Rahman, slain in a 1975 military coup, led Bangladesh to independence from Pakistan on December 16, 1971.

His daughter who took over as Prime Minister last June, 21 years after Awami League was ousted from power following Mujib's death, is presiding over a fortnight-long jubilee celebration, started on Sunday.

Hasina recently said that 86 pecent of Bangladesh's nearly 120 million people were unable to arrange "two nutritious meals a day," which she blamed mainly on previous corrupt and inefficient governments.
While renewing her firm pledge to generate employment through speedy industrialisation, she also vowed to end violence and terrorism.
"We are considering tougher laws to deal with murder and repression of women," she said, and added that "no killer will be allowed to go scot-free."
The prime minister expressed concern over what she called attempts by her foes to scuttle the development efforts.
"Some quarters are already engaged in conspiracy," she said without naming anyone, but clearly referring to the opposition Bangladesh nationalist Party (BNP) led by her predecessor Begum Khaleda Zia.

The BNP has threatened to overthrow Hasina if she went ahead with plans to buy electricity from India and grant New Delhi a right to transport goods to its northeastern states through Bangladesh territory.
Hasina said on Sunday that "power shortage is seriously threatening industrialisation and we must overcome it."
"We have to ensure power to industries. We will buy it from wherever it is available. I have no hestitation about it", she said.
Hasina earlier said the power shortfall was scaring away overseas investors, who will play a key role in its efforts for massive privatisation.
Hasina said she was also making effort to link Bangladesh with the proposed Asian Highway and Asian Railway. She gave no details.
